developments.title: Openings were steady; more workers quit
developments.facts: BLS reported September job openings of 7.5 million and hires of 5.4 million, both little changed. Quits increased to 3.4 million; layoffs and discharges were little changed at 1.6 million. August openings were revised to 7.2 million. The release was published November 3 at 10:00 AM ET.

impacts.interpretation: Stable reported openings and hiring sit alongside increased quits. Labor demand and wage pressure can move differently; one lagged survey does not settle growth or the next rate decision.
Broad-company earnings can be affected by both household demand and wage costs. The survey supplies a dated labor observation, not an S&P 500 earnings surprise or measured return.
Labor data can affect rate expectations and business demand, which may matter for technology valuations. These economy-wide counts do not measure technology hiring or a Nasdaq price reaction.
BLS reported a lower layoffs rate at establishments with 1–9 employees. That size class is not the Russell 2000; company margins, refinancing costs and actual small-cap prices remain separate inputs.
BLS identified more hiring in accommodation and food services. The sector mix may inform customer demand, but it is not a direct reading of hiring or margins across Dow constituents.
Stable openings alongside increased quits can leave competing interpretations of labor pressure. TLT depends on expected future rates and term premium; no long-yield response is measured here.

developments.limitation: Lagged, seasonally adjusted survey estimates that can be revised. Economist expectations, an employment-payroll surprise and instrument price reactions are not measured. Provenance correction: the citation now uses the dated BLS archive; the figures and interpretation are unchanged.

developments.title: Apple's new quarter updates the earnings picture
developments.facts: Apple reported $114.477bn revenue for the September 26 quarter, up from $102.466bn a year earlier. GAAP diluted EPS rose to $2.10 from $1.85. A tariff refund added $0.05 to EPS; that benefit is not recurring operating growth.

impacts.interpretation: Apple adds a newer consumer and technology earnings observation. Separate sales growth from the refund benefit when assessing the durability of margins.
Apple is one contributor to broad-market earnings. Its improved reported quarter does not establish whether the S&P 500 will rise or whether expectations were exceeded.
The sales and EPS comparison informs the technology earnings picture. The refund benefit warrants separating reported EPS growth from recurring business performance.
Apple contributes a company-specific demand signal for the Dow. Translating it into an index effect also requires prices and the other constituents.

developments.limitation: Selected company release. No independently verified analyst consensus, index-weight calculation or market-price response is included.

developments.title: Microsoft's growth comes with a GAAP distinction
developments.facts: Microsoft reported September-quarter revenue of $92.279bn, up from $77.673bn a year earlier. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.92; adjusted EPS was $4.89. The company reported 48% Azure revenue growth.

impacts.interpretation: Cloud growth is evidence of demand at one large supplier. It does not on its own measure economy-wide AI returns or justify current equity valuations.
Revenue growth supports the earnings backdrop for a major index constituent. The index impact still depends on expectations, valuation and other companies.
Azure growth informs the technology demand picture. Distinguish GAAP from adjusted EPS, and compare with a verified expectation before describing a beat.
Microsoft supplies a company-specific view of enterprise demand. Strong reported growth is not a measured next-session return for the Dow.

developments.limitation: Company-reported actuals. Analyst expectations, a verified earnings surprise and the market reaction are not measured.

developments.title: The Fed held rates; two members wanted a hike
developments.facts: On October 28, the Fed kept its target range at 3.75–4.00%. The vote was 10–2, with both dissenters preferring a quarter-point increase. The statement described inflation as elevated.

impacts.interpretation: A hold leaves the current policy target unchanged. The dissent highlights disagreement over inflation; it does not establish the direction of the next decision.
Policy rates influence financing costs and equity discount rates. The effect on the index depends on the path already priced and subsequent data.
Technology valuations can be sensitive to discount rates. An unchanged policy rate is not an unchanged long-term yield or a measured price response.
Small-company funding conditions depend partly on short-term rates and credit spreads. A hold leaves that policy-rate hurdle in place.
Rates affect company funding and customer demand through different channels. A single policy decision does not imply a uniform response across the Dow.
Long Treasuries respond to expected future rates and term premium, not only today's target. The hold alone is insufficient to infer TLT's next move.

developments.limitation: The official decision is known; future policy, priced expectations and instrument returns are not predictions in this review.

guidance.assumptions: Management stated its second-quarter outlook in US dollars. At then-current exchange rates, Microsoft expected no meaningful FX impact on total revenue growth. These expectations can differ from eventual results.

NVIDIA assumed no Data Center compute revenue from China in this outlook. The plus-or-minus 2% is the company’s guidance range, not a probability or confidence interval. These expectations can differ from eventual results.
